statement: HBM3E is described as effectively sold out for 2026 with prices up double digits year-over-year, and SK Hynix is said to hold about 62 percent of HBM4 supply and to provide roughly two-thirds of NVIDIA HBM4.
why: Memory sold out a year ahead with rising prices means HBM, not logic, sets how many accelerators can actually be built, and the dependence on one supplier makes that constraint fragile.

impact.mechanism: Sold-out HBM with rising prices caps accelerator build volumes and raises bill-of-materials cost, while single-supplier dependence adds concentration risk.

evidence.excerpt: HBM3E 'effectively sold out for 2026' with prices 'up double digits year-over-year'

confidence.basis: Secondary analyst brief relaying a second analyst source quoted inside the same document; publishers quoted within one document do not count toward corroboration.

dispersion: Price move is stated only as double digits year-over-year, so no percentage is recorded.
